issue.title: sase bead work aborts mid-cleanup after already wiping some forced-reuse targets
issue.description:
Discovered 2026-08-16 while relaunching stalled epic phase agents after the bead-store wedge.

Reproduction (observed once, then self-cleared):

  $ sase bead work sase-m6.6.1 -Y
  Existing agents for epic sase-m6.6.1:
    KILL     (WAITING) sase-m6.6.1.7 ...
    KILL     (WAITING) sase-m6.6.1.land ...
    REMOVE   (COMPLETED) sase-m6.6.1.6--code ...
    REMOVE   (MONITORED) sase-m6.6.1.6--mon ...
    REMOVE   (COMPLETED) sase-m6.6.1.6--plan ...
  Error: bead-work cleanup target sase-m6.6.1.6--code is no longer eligible for destructive cleanup

No agents launched. Re-running the identical command immediately succeeded, and its preview then listed only the two KILL targets -- the three REMOVE targets were already gone. So the first run wiped part of the selection, then aborted, leaving the epic with neither its old agents nor new ones. Nothing relaunched it; the operator had to notice and retry.

Root cause: _verify_cleanup_target_still_selected in src/sase/bead/cli_work_cleanup.py:858-901 re-validates each target against a freshly recomputed selection and raises ForcedReuseCleanupError when a target is no longer in destructive_targets. That check runs per target during the wipe loop, so targets already processed stay wiped when a later one fails. The guard itself is right (it is a TOCTOU check); the problem is that its failure is not atomic and not self-healing.

Impact: an epic relaunch can silently leave an epic with no live agents. During this incident that would have gone unnoticed had the retry not been run by hand -- the epic's phase agents simply would not exist.

Scope: make the destructive-cleanup phase all-or-nothing, or make the abort path either roll back or automatically re-drive the launch from the recomputed selection. The sibling error message on line 900 already says 'rerun', which suggests the retry was intended to be the operator's job; at minimum the partial-wipe case should say what was already removed and that the epic now has no agents.

payload.entry:
Fixed by epic sase-ns.6 phase sase-ns.6.3, commit 4d8d24eef 'fix(bead): make forced-reuse cleanup all-or-nothing'. Closed by that epic's land agent because the phase worker did not perform its plan-mandated bead bookkeeping.

FIX (src/sase/bead/cli_work_cleanup_apply.py, prepare_selected_bead_work_force_reuse): the verify and wipe passes are now separate loops. Every destructive target is checked by _verify_cleanup_target_still_selected before any target is wiped, so the reported failure mode -- a TOCTOU check firing on a later target after earlier targets were already destroyed -- can no longer destroy anything. The wipe loop additionally tracks wiped_names, and a genuine mid-wipe failure is re-raised as a ForcedReuseCleanupError naming which owners were already wiped and stating that the epic now has no live agent for them until the command is rerun. That matches the sibling 'rerun' guidance in revalidate_bead_work_launch_selection: retry stays the operator's job, but the error is now honest about the state it leaves behind.

REGRESSION COVERAGE: tests/test_bead/test_cli_work_cleanup_apply.py (3 tests) covers verify-before-wipe ordering (a stale later target aborts with zero wipes), the partial-wipe failure message content, and that a first-target failure leaves no stale claim.

VERIFICATION: phase sase-ns.6.3 ran the new tests plus the existing cleanup/confirm suites (17 passed) and a full 'just check' with every lint gate green. Re-verified by the land agent at HEAD 6000a54a1: tests/test_bead/test_cli_work_cleanup_apply.py plus tests/ace/tui/test_config_center_state.py -> 26 passed, and 'just check' exits 0.

RESIDUAL RISK, stated plainly: this does not close the window entirely. A wipe can still fail partway through, leaving earlier targets destroyed; the change converts that from a silent strand into a named, actionable error. Narrowing it further would need rollback or automatic re-drive of the launch, which the bead itself listed as the higher-risk alternative and which was not attempted.
